doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Cello group, family and the road
title: Children and the station-wagon road years
summary: Cutting to piano and two voices, touring with a baby in a station wagon, and sterilizing bottles in motels.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So after the kind of short lived group with the cello, did you consciously sit and say okay the public wasn’t quite ready for that, what are we going to do now.
In the interim, amidst all these things, we’re having kids, and having to deal with—

Having to do with just living in your life and you know, because and that’s been probably one of our problems in the sense of being known to the public, because every time we’d get a little momentum going, as far as having people know us more widely, we would have a family thing happen. It was wonderful. We were happy about it.

And it was — I was going to say what we did was cut down to just the two of us, just piano and the two voices, and we worked anywhere we could. Because things were rather slow. See a lot of clubs were closing, and we worked anywhere we could. And finally we got on the road with a child, and we had a station wagon with a rack on the top, and we had a kind of a buggy, and behind the back seat—

One of those that you lift out of the frame you know? And you put it behind the second seat in the station wagon and so if you have to change the baby you get on your knees and you’ve got your own little bassinet right there. And that was the days when you had to sterilize bottles and everything. Every night you’d check into a motel on a trip you know, and have to take the sterilizer in and wash the bottles and sterilize them. And luckily she was, by that time, just drinking milk rather than formula. And so I just had to fill the bottles. But still it was like ohh. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
This is reality, but thinking back on it, it was fun. It was like having to deal with it and we were young enough and had the energy and the will to do it.
